title: Linear transport of finite locally constant module stalks
statement: For any scheme Y and ring R, every natural isomorphism between finite locally constant set fibre functors induces a natural R-linear isomorphism on lisse R-module stalks, with the underlying-set evaluation formula. These maps form a linear path family. For finite rings they commute with the canonical balanced scalar stalk comparisons, giving a finite fibre path transport record as in [new-e5-fibre-path-transport-data]. A locally constant module sheaf with finite stalks is lisse. Definitions and hypotheses are those of [new-e5-fibre-path-transport-data], [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves].

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d), pp.146-147; Stacks Tag 0BND (2), Tag 0BN5; explicit part of the fibre transport argument

proof.text: Prove that a locally constant module sheaf with finite stalks has finite constant values on an etale trivialization, hence finitely generated module values. The underlying sheaf and its square are finite locally constant.

Transport set stalks by the given finite-set path. Naturality with projections identifies the transported product map; addition and the set maps x ↦ r*x prove additivity and R-linearity. Naturality gives the linear natural isomorphism, and component evaluation gives all four path laws.

For scalar extension use the stalk adjunction unit. On each germ, the underlying scalar unit is x ↦ 1 tensor x, so naturality of the set path gives the square on units. The scalar adjunction determines the whole linear map.
